prize_parts.citation: For the development of ionizable lipid nanoparticles that enable the systemic delivery of nucleic-acid medicines

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange I keep B040 as my single-part preference. The scientific core is a structure-property rule: an amino lipid whose apparent pKa is near-neutral in blood and cationic in the acidifying endosome, assembled with PEG-lipid and cargo by rapid mixing, so that a large polyanion survives circulation and then destabilises the endosomal membrane. That rule turned siRNA and later mRNA into usable medicines (patisiran, the COVID-19 vaccines) and has been confirmed independently at global scale, so maturity is settled. It also answers my test question, whether this changed what chemists and clinicians can do, more directly than any other shortlisted candidate. A citation written around ionizable lipid design and assembly, and not around vaccines, is complementary to the 2023 Medicine prize for nucleoside modification and does not repeat it. I would anchor the credit on the ionizable-lipid line: Cullis for the formulation concept and the Vancouver programme, MacLachlan for the optimised ionizable lipids that made systemic siRNA work, and Anderson for the lipidoid libraries that carried the approach to potent in vivo delivery and extended it to mRNA.
statement.case_against: The attribution remains the weakest point and I have not been able to resolve it from the record. Hope and Madden built the early Vancouver formulation work, Langer is central to delivery materials, and any three-name cut excludes people with serious claims. Aqvist and Somfai are right that part of the history is entangled with patents and company development that the committee cannot adjudicate from memory, and Chabes's Cullis, Madden and Hope trio is a defensible principled alternative if the committee decides the decisive step was the formulation, not the ionizable lipid. A secondary risk is that Academy readers see delivery as pharmaceutical engineering, or as a second prize for the mRNA story. If the field reports cannot name a defensible trio, B004 is the safer configuration and I would accept it without reservation about its merit.

responses.point: Somfai holds that C-N coupling is a distinct, mature and cleanly attributed two-person prize, that the ligand toolbox and amine-binding, deprotonation and reductive-elimination mechanism are new relative to 2010, and that B040 is a formulation technology with six contested names.
responses.response: The chair asked for the part of Buchwald and Hartwig's work that is distinct from the C-C precedent, and Somfai and Zou answer it convincingly: a different bond-forming step, a new ligand class, and a different chemical space. I now regard the 2010 overlap as a weak objection to B004 and I withdraw the weight I gave it earlier. What keeps me on B040 is not that B004 is unworthy but that B040 opened a modality, nucleic-acid delivery, that did not exist for chemists before, while B004 improves how a familiar bond is made. I also accept his attribution objection as the real cost of my choice. If the field reports cannot support a trio on B040, I would move to B004 with Buchwald and Hartwig alone and I would leave Kosugi to a mention in the text.

responses.point: Aqvist argues that the pKa-tuned ionizable lipid, from MacLachlan and Cullis and then Anderson, is what changed in vivo outcomes, and that credit should follow the ionizable lipid design and not the earlier liposome formulation, while admitting Hope and Madden are left out unfairly.
responses.response: I agree and this is the reasoning behind my trio. The step that made systemic delivery potent was the move from permanently cationic lipids to a titratable headgroup optimised by structure-activity work, and that is what ties the Vancouver programme to the products. I would add one caution to his argument. Cullis is the only name that sits on both lines, so a defensible configuration must keep him as anchor, and the choice of the other two depends on which reading of the decisive step the field reports support. I cannot verify the dates and the patent history, so I would ask the reports to state first demonstration of the pKa-tuned principle for in vivo delivery explicitly before the vote, as the chair requests.

responses.point: Chabes ranks B046 first as one principle of induced proximity, rests the case on mechanism and reproduction of the cereblon work, and proposes Cullis, Madden and Hope for B040 on chemistry-specific credit.
responses.response: His Cullis, Madden and Hope trio is the serious competing reading of B040 and I take it more seriously now than in round 1. It credits the formulation and rapid-mixing foundation, but it leaves out the ionizable-lipid optimisation that connects the work to approved products. On B046, I take his point that the cereblon mechanism has been reproduced repeatedly and that I should not lean on the clinical pipeline. I still cannot see one citation holding both the PROTAC concept and the cereblon discovery, and with Ciulli, Gray and Sakamoto outside the cap and no designed degrader approved, I keep it as an alternative, not the preferred part.

responses.point: Sparr, the committee's lipid assembly specialist, defends Cullis as anchor and MacLachlan for ionizable-lipid optimisation, calls Anderson's lipidoid libraries a distinct route, and says that excluding Hope and Madden is a choice about which step is decisive.
responses.response: Her framing is the most useful one on the table because it states the attribution as a scientific choice, not a fact. I agree that the lipid phase change on acidification, together with rapid mixing and PEG-lipid control of particle size, is what makes this chemistry rather than formulation. I would ask her to say whether Anderson's lipidoids are an independent discovery of ionizable-lipid design or a screening extension of the MacLachlan and Cullis principle, because that decides whether he belongs in the trio or whether Hope or Madden should take the slot. Like her, I flag that we both work near this field and may overweight it.

uncertainties: Which two of Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer should accompany Cullis; I cannot verify priority for the pKa-tuned ionizable lipid from memory and the field reports must settle it.
Whether the committee reads delivery as chemistry or as pharmaceutical engineering, and whether a prize close to the 2023 Medicine mRNA recognition will seem repetitive.
Whether Anderson's lipidoid work is an independent contribution or an extension of the Vancouver principle.
Whether B004 would be the safer vote if no majority forms around any B040 trio.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. I have no personal, institutional or mentoring tie to Cullis, MacLachlan, Anderson, Hope, Madden, Langer, Buchwald, Hartwig, Crews, Deshaies or Handa. My research on nanoparticle-biomolecule hybrids and biosensing is adjacent to nanomedicine, and I overlap with Emma Sparr on self-assembly; I regard neither as grounds for recusal, but I note that proximity to B040 could bias me and that I have tested my preference against B004.
